meta.description: Yes — Georgia O'Keeffe wrote it. The exact wording is documented in her 1976 autobiographical writing, echoing a 1926 catalogue foreword. Real, and in-copyright.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I found I could say things with color and shapes that I couldn't say any other way'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuinely Georgia O'Keeffe. Documented in her own 1976 writing, with an earlier 1926 catalogue variant. A rare quote that survives scrutiny intact.

answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: This is genuinely O’Keeffe’s own writing. The exact wording — “I found I could say things with color and shapes that I couldn’t say any other way — things I had no words for” — is documented in her 1976 autobiographical text, and a close variant appears as early as her 1926 Anderson Galleries catalogue foreword. It is not a fabrication.

source.heading: Where it comes from

docMeta.dd: Some Memories of Drawings (New York: Viking Press, 1976)
‘Foreword,’ Anderson Galleries exhibition catalogue, New York, 1926

source.excerpt: The abstraction is often the most definite form for the intangible thing in myself that I can only clarify in paint. … I found I could say things with color and shapes that I couldn’t say any other way — things I had no words for.
trail: The exact modern wording, with the closing clause “— things I had no words for,” is listed in the sourced section of O’Keeffe’s Wikiquote page, tied to her 1976 autobiographical text.
Wikiquote also records an earlier variant in her 1926 Anderson Galleries catalogue foreword: “I found that I could say things with colour and shapes that I couldn’t say in any other way…”
A widely-cited O’Keeffe quotes collection (unofficial) carries the same line, confirming it circulates as her genuine statement rather than an apocryphal one.
source.excerptNote: As documented in Wikiquote’s sourced section, which ties this wording to O’Keeffe’s 1976 Viking Press publication (Some Memories of Drawings) — though it does not cleanly pin a single page, and lists a near-identical line under her 1926 foreword.
source.rightsHolder: The Georgia O’Keeffe estate / Georgia O’Keeffe Museum; text first published 1976 by Viking Press
source.rightsNote: The exact published wording appears in O’Keeffe’s own 1976 book, so the text is in copyright in the United States. The underlying thought dates to her 1926 catalogue foreword, but that earlier phrasing differs; the polished sentence people quote today is the 1976 one.

author.name: Georgia O’Keeffe
author.heading: About Georgia O’Keeffe
author.bio: Georgia O’Keeffe was a pioneer of American modernism, celebrated for her magnified flowers, New York cityscapes, and the bleached bones and desert forms of New Mexico. She wrote sparingly but memorably about her work, and this line — about reaching for what words could not carry — is among her most quoted reflections on why she painted abstractly.

misattribution.heading: A real quote, but often mis-sourced
misattribution.intro: The attribution to O’Keeffe is correct — the common errors are about which source and how the sentence is trimmed.

items.why: Many sites pin the exact modern wording to O’Keeffe’s 1926 Anderson Galleries foreword. That 1926 text is a looser variant (“…that I could say things with colour and shapes that I couldn’t say in any other way”); the tidy version people quote matches her 1976 autobiographical writing.
The quote is usually cut off at “any other way,” dropping O’Keeffe’s own closing clause — “things I had no words for” — which is the point of the sentence.

misattribution.truthLine: The words are genuinely O’Keeffe’s; the exact published phrasing belongs to her 1976 writing, not the 1926 catalogue.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: O’Keeffe wrote the line to explain why she turned to abstraction. Trained in schools that taught her to paint as others did, she decided instead to paint what only she could see — and found that color and form could carry meaning that language could not.
The sentence has become a kind of manifesto for visual artists: a plain statement that some things are sayable only in paint.
